question: Who should decide how the most powerful AI systems are controlled: one company, one country, or many countries together?
reflection: Shared problems like disease and powerful technology are easier to solve when knowledge and responsibility are shared too.

sources.subject: Hackers steal OpenCode users' AI keys
Claude designs 318K proteins for scorpion antivenom autonomously

one_line: AI is starting to run the first stage of drug discovery on its own, while leaders openly debate who should control AI that becomes more capable than people.

top_stories.title: Claude designs candidate proteins against scorpion toxins
top_stories.what: Anthropic says a Claude research model designed over 318,000 small proteins aimed at scorpion toxins; of 211 tested in labs, 17 bound strongly to individual toxins, though none is yet proven to neutralise venom.
top_stories.why: It shows AI can shrink the slow early search in drug discovery, which matters for neglected regional health problems.

top_stories.title: Three possible futures for controlling powerful AI
top_stories.what: OpenAI's CEO reportedly told staff the industry has discussed an international watchdog, a shared research body, or one dominant company, and called the last option terrible.
top_stories.why: Middle powers have a direct interest in which governance model wins, since it decides who gets access to frontier systems.

top_stories.title: US government removes DeepSeek from federal systems
top_stories.what: The US ordered civilian agencies to stop buying DeepSeek products and remove them, including third-party tools built on its technology, citing security risks.
top_stories.why: Public bodies everywhere are being pushed to know exactly which models sit inside the tools they buy, which makes AI supply-chain audits a growing need.

saudi_lens.text: Scorpion stings are a real public-health issue in the Arabian Peninsula, so AI-designed binders, if they pass further testing, could interest Saudi health and research bodies.
Saudi agencies that buy AI products may need a simple inventory of which underlying models each tool uses, as procurement rules tighten worldwide.

idea.title: AI model inventory for public agencies
idea.pitch: A short audit method that maps every AI tool an agency uses to its underlying model, vendor and data location.
idea.first_step: List the AI-enabled tools one department uses and ask each vendor which model powers it.
